t: Built from 1406 to 1420, the palace was the ceremonial and political centre of the Chinese government for over 500 years.
Its layout, colours and numbers were planned to express imperial majesty and the order of heaven and earth.
Since 1925 it has been the Palace Museum, whose collections grew from the Ming and Qing imperial collections.
dyk: A common story says the palace has 9,999 rooms, but survey evidence counts 8,886 bays of rooms in 980 surviving buildings.
ev: Construction begins after the Yongle Emperor moves the capital from Nanjing to Beijing
The palace becomes the seat of the Ming dynasty
Li Zicheng captures the palace and sets fire to parts of it as he flees; the Qing proclaim the Shunzhi Emperor there
Anglo-French forces occupy the palace during the Second Opium War
The abdication of Puyi ends its role as the political centre of China
The Palace Museum is established after Puyi's eviction in 1924
Part of the evacuated collection is shipped to Taiwan under orders of Chiang Kai-shek
UNESCO declares it a World Heritage Site as the Imperial Palace of the Ming and Qing Dynasties

f.made: Built for the Yongle Emperor of the Ming dynasty, who moved the capital from Nanjing to Beijing; construction took 14 years and more than a million workers; altered by the Qing rulers
f.form: A walled rectangle 961 m by 753 m with a moat, holding 980 surviving buildings with 8,886 bays of rooms, chiefly of wood on marble terraces, divided into an Outer Court and an Inner Court
f.where: The centre of Beijing, administered by the Palace Museum; part of the former imperial collection is in the National Palace Museum in Taipei
f.known: residence of 24 Ming and Qing emperors; the Hall of Supreme Harmony; yellow glazed roofs; the central north-south axis of Beijing; the Palace Museum's collections; a World Heritage Site since 1987
